answer: Each identity registers one vertex on the copper grid and locks an 80-credit bond, filing its feeder and wire length. An auditor sends an ember pulse through that vertex; the identity must return a reading matching the copper table for its feeder, or the bond burns. The first filing costs 35 credits; the kth filing by one operator costs 35+5(k-1), so the 1000th costs 5030 and 1000 fakes pay 2,532,500 in fees plus 80,000 locked. A rented-vertex ring fails: one feeder cannot give distinct readings for two vertices, so duplicates burn both bonds. An honest agent pays one bond and one 35 fee.
